messages.content: Could you retrieve the 10-day weather forecast for the campsite at 35.68 latitude and -121.34 longitude, including daily temperature in Fahrenheit and total precipitation in inches?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

We need to call the function requests_get. Provide URL, headers, params. The API likely is NWS API. We need to get forecast for given lat/lon. The NWS API endpoint: https://api.weather.gov/gridpoints/{office}/{gridX},{gridY}/forecast?format=json. But we don't have office and grid coordinates. Alternatively use /points/{lat},{lon}/forecast?format=json. That returns forecast periods. We need 10-day forecast. The forecast includes periods with startTime, endTime, temperature, temperatureUnit, windSpeed, windDirection, shortForecast, detailedForecast, etc. Precipitation is not directly given; maybe precipitation probability. But the user wants total precipitation in inches. The NWS API does not provide precipitation amounts. Might need to use another API like NOAA Climate Data Online or other. But maybe we can approximate using precipitation probability and average rainfall? Not possible.

Alternatively use WeatherAPI.com or OpenWeatherMap. But we don't have API keys. The tool may allow us to fetch from open APIs. Let's try to use Open-Meteo API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=35.68&longitude=-121.34&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum&timezone=auto. That returns daily max/min temps and precipitation sum in mm. We can convert to Fahrenheit and inches. So we can call that.

Thus we need to call requests_get with url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Headers: Accept: application/json. Params: lat=35.68, lon=-121.34, daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum, timezone=auto, forecast_days=10? Actually open-meteo uses "forecast_days" param? The API uses "daily" and "start_date" "end_date". We can specify "start_date" today and "end_date" 10 days ahead. But we can just request daily=... and let it return up to 7 days? Actually open-meteo returns up to 30 days by default? Let's check. The API supports "forecast_days" param. We'll set forecast_days=10. Also "temperature_unit" param? The default is Celsius. We can set "temperature_unit=fahrenheit". And "precipitation_unit=inch"? The API supports "precipitation_unit=inch". So we can set those. So final params: lat=35.68, lon=-121.34, daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum, timezone=auto, forecast_days=10, temperature_unit=fahrenheit, precipitation_unit=inch.

Thus we call function.
